target_customer: Families with children in San Francisco who book guided adventures at about 15 dollars per person
problem: Families want screen-free outdoor activities for kids, and location-based experiences are hard to produce at scale.
business_model: Ticketed location-based AR scavenger hunts with live actors, 15 dollars per person

founders.name: Jeany Ngo
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch 2019-03-14. Background not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Brian Schulman
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder. A Marketscreener listing (seen in search only) calls him founder and CTO. Background not found.

competitors.name: Sandbox VR
competitors.traction_then: Cited by TechCrunch as a comparable location-based experience
competitors.funding_then: 68 million dollar Series B led by a16z, per TechCrunch

competitors.name: Seek
competitors.what: AR treasure hunting app that pivoted to an AR projects hub
competitors.traction_then: Launched at SXSW, consumer app with real rewards

technical_complexity.rationale: Geo-tagged AR tasks plus live actor scheduling and content production for each hunt. Standard mobile AR tooling in 2019, but content and operations were heavy for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Hunts are content and operations that rivals could copy. No data, network or regulatory moat described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch compared it with Pokemon GO but noted that product lacks linear stories. No incumbent action found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2019-03-14) quoted the founder on parents wanting alternatives to screen time. Tickets were 15 dollars per person for 45 to 60 minute hunts in Chinatown and Golden Gate Park. No demand data beyond that.

branding.domain_note: Uses adventurous.co, a .co domain, not the .com. The site returned a 503 on fetch.

brand_strength.rationale: Name conveys the product but is generic and hard to search. No press on the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Adventurous launched family AR scavenger hunts in San Francisco in early 2019 and was covered by TechCrunch during its YC batch, but no funding, shutdown announcement or post-mortem was found. The company is listed Inactive by YC, and a later directory description suggests it may have shifted toward local family events. The cause of the stall is not public, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: A CB Insights entity named Adventure Hunt shows a 150K angel round in January 2019; not linked to this company by any source, so not recorded. Employbl (updated Nov 2025) describes kids and family adventures, possibly a later direction; unverified. Cause of inactivity is not public.
